findings_to_judge.finding: Q1 FY27 consensus revenue is $237.99M, roughly 7% below what Methode's own disclosed FY27 building blocks imply for the quarter (Q1 FY26 base of $240.5M, plus the guided data-centre ramp from ~$80M to ~$130M i.e. ~+$12M/quarter, plus North American automotive going from $182M to ~$200M), and the same model was at $238.46M against a $298.1M actual last quarter and $224.57M against a $240.5M actual in the year-ago quarter.

Every external datapoint bearing on Methode's two growth lines post-dates the 25 June guide: hyperscaler 2026 capex was raised across the board in late July (Amazon $200B to $220B, Alphabet $180-190B to $195-205B, Meta narrowed up), and GM raised its own FY26 EBIT guidance by $500M on 21 July while running Flint Assembly six days a week from June on heavy-duty pickup demand - while Methode's data-centre number is built only on existing vendor-managed busbar volume with the 800VDC rack architecture explicitly excluded from guidance by management.

Q4 FY26's headline was inflated by $22.5M of non-recurring customer recoveries recognised as revenue, so adjusted EBITDA of $26.9M on 24.2% gross margin sat on roughly $275.6M of underlying revenue and only single-digit-millions of underlying EBITDA; management said recovery activity is 'largely done' and excluded the remaining balance from FY27 guidance, so this print delivers the year's worst sequential optics - revenue down ~15% and EBITDA down sharply from Q4 - into a stock at a 52-week high.

Exactly one year ago Methode postponed this same fiscal quarter's release on the scheduled release day - 3 September 2025, having pre-announced 3 September on 21 August 2025 - gave no reason whatsoever in the reschedule notice, and the stock fell 11.4% the following session; it then reported six days later, on 9 September 2025, with a revenue beat ($240.5M vs $224.57M) and an EPS beat (-$0.22 vs -$0.40).

Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $26.9M (9.0% margin) versus Q3 FY26's $7.3M (3.1% margin) is a $19.6M sequential jump that is almost exactly the ~$19M of one-time EV customer recoveries management said flowed through to earnings; ex-recoveries Q4 margin was ~2.9%, i.e. flat with Q3, and the FY27 guide of $72-82M adj EBITDA is therefore +47% to +67% off a recovery-adjusted FY26 base of ~$49M, not the +6% to +20% the headline $68.2M comparison implies.

The +16.5% five-session run-up happened entirely AFTER the only piece of news: Craig-Hallum's initiation moved the stock +14.9% on 2026-08-25 to $16.05, and it then closed up four straight sessions (~17.06, 17.78, 18.23, 18.32, 18.705) on rising volume with no company release in that window other than the 26 Aug earnings-date notice - leaving spot above Baird's $16 target and at 86% of the $22 average target going into a quarter the company guided to be the seasonally weak one.

SemiAnalysis's deep supply-chain teardown of the 800VDC rack transition does not mention Methode Electronics anywhere, and names TE Connectivity for the standardized busbars in the Diablo 400 specification alongside Delta, ABB, Legrand and EAE for 800VDC distribution.
